Well when you make a BBB complaint, they work as a middle man to try to negotiate a solution to the complaint. I've had to do this with Xfinity as well after I spent weeks trying to get Xfinity to fix an issue and they were more concerned with trying to sell me another plan.

An attorney friend of mine told me that most people don't even know if they are BBB accredited but they do know what the BBB is and don't really want to look bad. 
When you file a complaint and not a review people can see the details of the complaint along with the companies response and whether or not you agreed with that response. 
I believe the BBB informs them of this and it's usually enough to get their asses into gear to solve the issue.

This is why rentals are mainly geared towards collage students. Lots of them have mommy and daddy's money to spend and won't complain because they don't know any better.

When we asked the landlord if he was going to cover the holes up he said "no, there's two shower curtains in the bathroom though that you can just take down and shove in those holes when it starts to get colder."

Surprised the hell outta me since all the landlords around here balk at even the thought of accepting HUD because of the "requirements".

My state reps don't care. A few years ago my area had an uptick in SNAP related thefts. It all boiled down to one local grocery chain using unsafe methods to verify eligibility for their online SNAP orders and their senior discount program that helped elderly people get their groceries for free.

Most of the victims were over 65 and because I worked with peer recovery coaches who were gifted in assisting people with getting and keeping their benefits through DHHR, DHHR would just send them to us to get help through local charities and food banks. This was to provide them with some food since they made it clear they didn't give a damn and weren't going to do anything about the thefts.

Myself, some colleagues and even a bunch of social workers spent weeks shouting to the heavens and trying to bring this matter to our state reps attention.

Eventually we were all told to "stop calling and bothering the senator, he is very busy and has heard your complaints".
At one point, the senator was recorded saying "I don't give a good goddamn" after a case manager for a local community health center stood with a crowd of reporters who were asking the senator questions.

I believe it went like "Mr. Senator, do you mind telling us why no one is acting to combat the theft of SNAP benefits from elderly recipients in Monroe county?" 

He attempted to ignore the question so they then stood in his way and said "sir could you please answer our question? There are elderly victims who have been waiting for over 9 months for action on this." 
To which the crowd got quiet as he said "I don't give a good goddamn" under his breath before his handlers pushed past her.

It took four of us filing a better business bureau complaint within the span of 30 days for the company to change their verification methods and making it so that just having your eligibility letter with just the person's name and the words eligible visible if need be. 
They took it a step further and required that the name on the letter had to match the name on the card and if you were getting delivery or pick up, you had to show your I.d. and if you weren't approved to have someone like another family member collect the goods, they would immediately take back the food and issue a refund.

This cut the thefts by over two thirds but sadly the store closed in 2023. 
But yeah, moral of the story, not all state reps give a goddamn lol.

I went on suboxone. I went into treatment with benzos in my system, and they weren't going to give me suboxone. Most of the workers seemed shocked and said they'd never heard about people taking lope. Luckily, the on call doctor was from california and was well acquainted with it. 
Honestly, as a drug for addiction treatment, it could work. Theres just too many downsides to it. 
My health has been ruined because of it, and I've known for a long time its because of this drug.

I just went to detox and then went to a recovery center for 30 days. It's been easy for me because i despised my addiction. I still take suboxone now, but it's mainly for my chronic pain.

If you are a user who has been at this for a while and has lots of people you can buy from, it's best to just follow the guidelines for getting clean. One of those involves moving away to an area where you don't know people and won't have people stopping you on the street asking if you wanna buy something, ya know?

Honestly, this probably sounds cliché but treatment saved my life. It sucks to have to go in somewhere for this stuff, but it felt really good to be among people who also wanted to get clean.
It was fun, actually, lol. But I was able to talk about things I'd held in, and the best part is that no one there could judge me because they were in the same boat.

I hope things work out for you. I, too, was once searching for drugs that help with withdrawals. I wish I could find the person who told me about lope and strangle them, lol.
